newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian businessman fires at parked airliner.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian businessman fires at parked airliner.

text.p: Prominent Cambodian businessman Teng Boonma shot at a tyre of a parked airliner at Phnom Penh airport after a dispute over schedules and lost luggage, witnesses and officials said on Tuesday.

No one was injured but a front wheel of the Royal Air Cambodge Boeing 737-400, on which Teng Boonma had been a passenger on a flight from Hong Kong, was damaged and had to be replaced, officials said.
There were staff on the aircraft when the shooting occurred, but all the passengers had disembarked.

"I was furious, so I shot one tyre. Of course I wanted to shoot four tyres in order to pay them back," said Teng Boonma, who is head of the Phnom Penh Chamber of Commerce and managing director of the powerful Thai Boon Roong Group.
He told Reuters he was angry because the flight was late, the pilot was rude to him when he boarded at the last minute in Hong Kong, and the airline lost his luggage.
He said the luggage was worth $2,000 but the airline offered him only $200 to replace it.
Royal Air Cambodge Chairman Vichit Ith expressed concern over the incident and said he did not understand Teng Boonma's anger because the flight had been five minutes early.
He said no complaints had been received from any of the other passengers on the approximately 2-3/4 hour flight.

"I am going to turn (the matter over) to the government because there is serious concern for our passengers," he told Reuters. "We could not accept that such a thing could happen again -- to our airplanes, our staff or our passengers."
He said several staff were on the aircraft when the shooting occurred and there was some fuel in the tanks.
Teng Boonma told Reuters he stopped shooting because he was worried the bullets would wound others.
King Samnang, deputy chief of Cambodia's Interpol department, said he was submitting a report on the incident to the Ministry of Interior.

He said Teng Boonma fired a Russian automatic weapon belonging to his bodyguard, who had met his boss in the VIP lounge area. After taking the weapon from the bodyguard, Teng Booma went back onto the tarmac and opened fire.
Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh condemned the incident but assured travellers the airport was safe.
"We never see this anywhere in the world but Cambodia," he told reporters and urged the authorities to investigate the incident promptly.
"This situation of Cambodia is becoming worse and worse. It is completely anarchic for Cambodians," he said, adding measures had to be taken by the relevant authorities.
As Ranariddh concluded his remarks, shots rang out across the street in what police said was a neighbourhood dispute.
"You see!" Ranariddh said as he left.

Teng Boonma is reputedly Cambodia's wealthiest businessman, with interests that include the newly opened Intercontinental Hotel, trading companies and the Cambodia Mekong Bank. He is close to Ranariddh's rival and co-premier, Hun Sen.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who formed an uneasy coalition after the United Nations-sponsored polls of 1993, have already begun squaring off ahead of local and national elections this year and next.

On March 30, a deadly grenade attack on an opposition rally killed 19 people and wounded more than 100. Ranariddh told Reuters later he feared the attack was a prelude of more violence as the bruising campaign unfolds.
